body:
Quantum computers will break a lot of modern crypto, so I suggest we change:

6.2.4 | Verify that random number, encryption or hashing algorithms, key lengths, rounds, ciphers or modes, can be reconfigured, upgraded, or swapped at any time, to protect against cryptographic breaks. (C8) |   | ✓ | ✓ | 326
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --

to:

6.2.4	Verify that random number, encryption or hashing algorithms, key lengths, rounds, ciphers or modes, can be reconfigured, upgraded, or swapped at any time, to protect against cryptographic breaks and the future of quantum computing. ([C8](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering))		✓	✓	326

comments.body: Can we have some argumentation behind that as well? I have heard the same sentence over 15+ years already.

Quantum computing is coming in about 6 years. 2030 is the “quantum horizon” yet we do not have good post-quantum computing algorithms available.

However, dev’s can get ready now by making sure we have crypto algorithm agility; ie: the ability to swap out algorithms and re-encrypt/re-sign data now in preparation for future algorithm changes that will be required when quantum computing is here.

This is a *very* basic concept and my suggestion is very minor here. I just want a brief mention of quantum in this requirement since it’s coming sooner than many think.
I prefer we don't try to predict future and we address the topic when we know exactly what is the threat then and what must be done to mitigate it.
Quantum was also mentioned in #1411. I am going to keep this as a reminder for the rework activity.
Ok I think #1411 is going to become the primary issue for reworking V6 so I am going to close this issue if that is ok with you @jmanico
